  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo .   search returns, by default: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as complete function bodies),
  RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus the other tests that cover the same code (ALSO COVERING —
  they all have to keep passing), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the queried concept is
  named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC — the sweep, so you need no grep), VERIFY (the narrowest test
  command for the file, derived from the repo's own build files) and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a
  switch over an enum/sealed set would throw at runtime rather than fail to compile. The three
  reference blocks — container map, signature types, declaration card — are OFF by default because
  they measurably cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all (or the individual flags,
  or ENTIRE_GRAPH_REFERENCE_BLOCKS) turns them back on for interactive reading.
  search --top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the
  exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every
  eligible file). neighbors/impact take --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME with
  --file/--line/--kind, to select one definition when a name is ambiguous; the ambiguity
  error prints the exact selector for each definition it found.

  its associated-function/method surface, drawn from the graph's own membership edges (inherent
  impl blocks, receiver methods, extension members, partial parts, one hop of trait/module/base

  implements it. Membership is never inferred from a name resembling another name.
  stats is a local read-only report for humans: it reads the coding-agent session transcripts
  already on disk (~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl) and reports graph usage vs
  grep/read exploration, bytes each pulled into context, and an ESTIMATED token saving whose
  assumption is printed with the number. --transcript narrows it to ONE session transcript
  (plus that session's subagent transcripts) instead of a whole project directory.

243	func runProviderRecords(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string, mode string) error {
244		flags, rest, err := parseProviderFlags(args)
245		if err != nil {
246			return err
247		}
248		if len(rest) != 0 {
249			return fmt.Errorf("%s received unexpected arguments: %s", mode, strings.Join(rest, " "))
250		}
251		if flags.Format != "ndjson" {
252			return fmt.Errorf("%s requires --format ndjson", mode)
253		}
254		repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, flags.Repo)
255		if err != nil {
256			return err
257		}
258		if mode != "snapshot" && mode != "symbols" && mode != "edges" {
259			return fmt.Errorf("unknown provider record mode %q", mode)
260		}
261		profile, err := parseProfile(flags.Profile)
262		if err != nil {
263			return err
264		}
265		options := sem.ProviderSnapshotOptions{
266			NoNetwork:    flags.NoNetwork,
267			Worktree:     flags.Worktree,
268			IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFiles,
269			IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFiles,
270			Profile:      profile,
271		}
272		if flags.Progress {
273			options.Progress = func(event sem.ProgressEvent) {
274				fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "graph progress phase=%s files=%d/%d symbols=%d relations=%d heap=%d rss=%d elapsed=%s\n",
275					event.Phase,
276					event.FilesDone,
277					event.FilesTotal,
278					event.Symbols,
279					event.Relations,
280					event.HeapAlloc,
281					event.MaxRSSBytes,
282					event.Elapsed.Round(time.Millisecond),
283				)
284			}
285		}
286		// Stream records straight to stdout so peak memory does not scale with the
287		// relation count on large repositories.
288		encoder := json.NewEncoder(opts.Stdout)
289		encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false) // match json.Marshal used elsewhere (no < escaping)
290	
291		// Targeted edge query: when --to/--from/--relation is set, emit only matching
292		// relations (plus header/summary), never files/symbols. Turns "callers of X"
293		// into a tiny reply instead of dumping the whole graph for the caller to grep.
294		// Streaming-safe: idMatches keys off the stable ID's trailing name segment, so
295		// no in-memory symbol table is needed. Only meaningful in edges/snapshot modes.
296		// Capture the summary as it streams past so we can loudly warn on a partial
297		// parse. Without this the CLI discards the summary and a run that silently
298		// parsed only a fraction of the repo (e.g. a mis-scoped subdir) looks clean.
299		var summary *sem.SnapshotSummary
300		capture := func(record any) {
301			if s, ok := record.(sem.SnapshotSummary); ok {
302				s := s
303				summary = &s
304			}
305		}
306	
307		filterActive := flags.To != "" || flags.From != "" || len(flags.Relation) > 0
308		if filterActive && mode == "symbols" {
309			return fmt.Errorf("--to/--from/--relation filter relations; use `edges` (not `symbols`)")
310		}
311		if filterActive {
312			var matched int
313			if err := sem.StreamSnapshot(ctx, repo, opts.Version, options, func(record any) error {
314				capture(record)
315				switch r := record.(type) {
316				case sem.RelationRecord:
317					if !relationMatches(r, flags) {
318						return nil
319					}
320					matched++
321					return encoder.Encode(r)
322				case sem.FileRecord, sem.ExternalRecord, sem.SymbolRecord:
323					return nil // suppressed for a targeted edge query
324				default: // header, summary
325					return encoder.Encode(record)
326				}
327			}); err != nil {
328				return err
329			}
330			warnIfPartial(opts.Stderr, flags.Worktree, summary)
331			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "graph: %d edge(s) matched (--to=%q --from=%q --relation=%s)\n",
332				matched, flags.To, flags.From, strings.Join(flags.Relation, ","))
333			return nil
334		}
335	
336		// Whole-graph dump (no targeted filter): serve from the tree-hash record
337		// cache when possible. The cache is keyed on the HEAD tree, the mode, and the
338		// output-affecting options, so a repeat call on an unchanged HEAD skips the
339		// expensive re-index. It is deliberately bypassed for --worktree (the working
340		// tree may differ from HEAD) and, by returning above, for targeted queries.
341		cacheDir := resolveCacheDir(flags.CacheDir, opts.Env.PluginDataDir)
342		useCache := !flags.DisableCache && !flags.Worktree && cacheDir != ""
343		var tree string
344		if useCache {
345			if t, err := gitutil.RevParse(ctx, repo, "HEAD^{tree}"); err == nil && t != "" {
346				tree = t
347			} else {
348				useCache = false
349			}
350		}
351		if useCache {
352			if records, cachedSummary, hit, err := sem.LoadProviderRecords(ctx, repo, opts.Version, tree, mode, cacheDir, options); err == nil && hit {
353				if _, err := opts.Stdout.Write(records); err != nil {
354					return err
355				}
356				warnIfPartial(opts.Stderr, flags.Worktree, cachedSummary)
357				return nil
358			}
359		}
360	
361		// On a miss, tee the streamed NDJSON into a buffer so we can persist it after
362		// a successful run without a second pass over the graph.
363		var recordBuf bytes.Buffer
364		if useCache {
365			encoder = json.NewEncoder(io.MultiWriter(opts.Stdout, &recordBuf))
366			encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
367		}
368		if err := sem.StreamSnapshot(ctx, repo, opts.Version, options, func(record any) error {
369			capture(record)
370			if !includeRecord(mode, record) {
371				return nil
372			}
373			return encoder.Encode(record)
374		}); err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		warnIfPartial(opts.Stderr, flags.Worktree, summary)
378		if useCache {
379			// Best effort: a failed cache write never fails the command.
380			_ = sem.StoreProviderRecords(ctx, repo, opts.Version, tree, mode, cacheDir, options, recordBuf.Bytes(), summary)
381		}
382		return nil
383	}

385	// warnIfPartial prints a loud stderr banner when the snapshot did not fully cover
386	// the repository, so a silent partial parse (the #1 sharp edge: running in a
387	// mis-scoped subdir without --worktree, which indexes only a stray config file
388	// and reports "ok") becomes impossible to miss. Silent on a clean "ok" run.
389	func warnIfPartial(w io.Writer, worktree bool, s *sem.SnapshotSummary) {
390		if s == nil {
391			return
392		}
393		level := s.Stats.CompletenessLevel
394		if level == "" || level == "ok" {
395			return
396		}
397		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n⚠️  graph is %s: parsed %d/%d files, %d symbols, %d relations (languages: %s).\n",
398			strings.ToUpper(level), s.Stats.ParsedFiles, s.Stats.Files, s.Stats.Symbols,
399			s.Stats.Relations, strings.Join(s.Languages, ", "))
400		switch {
401		case s.Stats.Files <= 2 && !worktree:
402			fmt.Fprintf(w, "   Only %d file(s) were discovered — you may be indexing a subdirectory or an\n"+
403				"   unexpected commit. Run from the repo root, or pass --worktree to index the\n"+
404				"   working tree instead of HEAD.\n", s.Stats.Files)
405		case s.Stats.ParsedFiles*2 < s.Stats.Files:
406			fmt.Fprintf(w, "   Over half the discovered files were not parsed (unsupported language or\n"+
407				"   parse errors). Graph queries will miss code in those files.\n")
408		default:
409			fmt.Fprintf(w, "   The graph is incomplete; treat query results as partial.\n")
410		}
411	}

469	// idMatches reports whether a stable symbol ID matches a user-supplied selector:
470	// either the exact ID, or a trailing name segment (IDs end `...:kind:name`, so
471	// `getConfPath` or `function:getConfPath` both select it). Streaming-safe — no
472	// symbol table needed.
473	func idMatches(id, sel string) bool {
474		return id == sel || strings.HasSuffix(id, ":"+sel)
475	}

477	// relationMatches applies the --to/--from/--relation predicate to one edge.
478	func relationMatches(r sem.RelationRecord, f providerFlags) bool {
479		if f.To != "" && !idMatches(r.ToID, f.To) {
480			return false
481		}
482		if f.From != "" && !idMatches(r.FromID, f.From) {
483			return false
484		}
485		if len(f.Relation) > 0 {
486			t := strings.ToUpper(r.Type)
487			hit := false
488			for _, want := range f.Relation {
489				if t == want {
490					hit = true
491					break
492				}
493			}
494			if !hit {
495				return false
496			}
497		}
498		return true
499	}

# Plan: Restructure `entire graph` help output

## Context

`entire graph` is a hand-rolled CLI (`internal/cli/`, dispatched in `root.go:Run`).
Its help has two problems:

1. **The root help is one dense blob.** `printHelp` (`root.go:103-164`) prints a flat
   `Usage:` list where every flag is inlined onto one long line per command, followed by a
   wall of `Notes:` prose. It is hard to scan and is not organized by what the user is trying
   to do.
2. **There is no per-command help.** `entire graph search --help`,
   `neighbors --help`, etc. all fail — `--help`/`-h` falls through flag parsing into `rest`
   and errors as an "unexpected argument". Every reference tool we compared
   (`gh`, `entire` itself via Cobra, `mise` via clap) supports `<cmd> --help` with a
   dedicated per-command layout (USAGE / FLAGS / ARGUMENTS / EXAMPLES).

Goal: a scannable, grouped root listing organized by user intent, plus real per-command help
for every subcommand and its parameters — matching the two-column, sectioned style of `gh`
and the installed `entire` CLI.

## Reference styles we're matching

- **`gh`**: short description → `USAGE` → command groups in CAPS headers → aligned
  `name: description` two-column list → per-command `FLAGS`/`ARGUMENTS`/`EXAMPLES`.
- **`entire` (Cobra)**: intro → `Getting Started` → grouped `Available Commands` (aligned) →
  `Flags` → footer `Use "entire [command] --help" for more information about a command.`

We adopt: aligned two-column command list under intent-based group headers, a footer hint,
and a per-command detail view.

## Design: a small doc registry (single source of truth)

New file `internal/cli/help.go`:

```go
type flagDoc struct{ name, arg, def, desc string } // e.g. "--top-k", "N", "10", "how many results"
type argDoc  struct{ name, desc string }
type commandDoc struct {
    name     string
    group    cmdGroup   // Setup | Inspect | Analyze
    summary  string     // one line, shown in the root list
    usage    []string   // one or more usage lines
    long     string     // detail paragraph(s) — absorbs today's Notes prose
    args     []argDoc
    flags    []flagDoc
    examples []string
}

var commandDocs = []commandDoc{ ... }   // ordered; one entry per dispatched command
```

Two renderers + a helper, also in `help.go`:
- `renderRootHelp(w io.Writer)` — intro line, then group sections in fixed order, each an
  aligned `name  summary` two-column block (compute the pad width from the longest name),
  then the footer hint. Replaces the body of `printHelp`.
- `renderCommandHelp(w io.Writer, name string)` — `Usage:`, `Arguments:` (if any),
  `Flags:` (aligned `--flag <arg>  desc (default: X)`), `Examples:`, and the `long`
  description. This is where the current dense `Notes:` content moves — split per command
  (search prose → search doc, def prose → def doc, stats prose → stats doc, etc.).
- `wantsHelp(args []string) bool` — true if any arg is `--help`/`-h`.

## Root grouping (per the request)

Three intent-based groups, in this order:

1. **Set up your agent** — the graph-with-an-agent basics:
   `init-agents`, `agent-guide`, `index`, `doctor`, `capabilities`
2. **Inspect the graph** — the query surface:
   `search`, `neighbors`, `impact`, `def`, `symbols`, `edges`, `snapshot`
3. **Analyze changes & more** — change/risk + reporting + meta:
   `commit`, `diff` (with `analyze` noted as an alias), `checkpoint`, `stats`, `version`

Root footer: `Use "entire graph <command> --help" for details on a command.`

## Wiring into dispatch (`root.go`)

- `printHelp(out)` → delegates to `renderRootHelp(out)` (keep the name; `root_test.go`
  and callers at `root.go:47,96` still reference it).
- Centralize help interception in `Run` so no `runX` needs editing: after `args[0]`
  matches a known command, if `wantsHelp(args[1:])`, call `renderCommandHelp(opts.Stdout,
  args[0])` and return nil. Keep the existing special cases for `help`/`--help`/`-h`
  (root) and `version`.
- Unknown-command path (`root.go:99`): keep the error but append a hint to run
  `entire graph help`.

No changes to flag *parsing* or command behavior — this is help/UX only.

## Files to touch

- `internal/cli/help.go` — **new**: `commandDoc` registry + `renderRootHelp` +
  `renderCommandHelp` + `wantsHelp` + alignment helper.
- `internal/cli/root.go` — shrink `printHelp` to delegate; add the `wantsHelp`
  interception in `Run`; tweak the unknown-command hint. Remove the inline `Usage:`/`Notes:`
  literal (content relocates into the registry).
- `internal/cli/root_test.go` — replace `TestHelpDocumentsNeighborAgentContextCap`
  (`:421-436`, it greps the old inline `entire graph neighbors ... --max-context-bytes
  16384` line) with an assertion against `renderCommandHelp` output for `neighbors`.

## Tests to add (`internal/cli/help_test.go`)

- **Registry ↔ dispatch parity**: the set of command names in `commandDocs` equals the set
  of cases handled in `Run`'s switch (guards against future drift — a new command with no
  help, or a stale doc, fails the test).
- **Root help**: every dispatched command name appears; the three group headers appear in
  order.
- **Per-command help**: `Run(..., []string{"search", "--help"})` returns nil and emits a
  `Usage:` + `Flags:` block; `neighbors --help` still documents `--max-context-bytes`
  default `16384` (preserves the intent of the deleted test).

## Verification

```sh
mise run build
./entire-graph                       # grouped root help, three sections
./entire-graph help                  # same
./entire-graph search --help         # per-command detail (usage/flags/examples)
./entire-graph neighbors --help      # shows --max-context-bytes default 16384
./entire-graph frobnicate            # unknown-cmd error + "run entire graph help" hint
mise run test                        # ./... incl. new help_test.go + updated root_test.go
mise run check                       # fmt + vet + race + build
```

Manual scan check: confirm each group lists the right commands and that the previously
buried `Notes:` guidance (search blocks, def semantics, cache defaults, `--max-seconds`,
`--include-file` behavior) now reads under the matching command's `--help`.

## Out of scope

- No change to command behavior, flag names, defaults, or output of the commands themselves.
- No shell-completion generation (could be a follow-up now that a registry exists).
- Not migrating to Cobra — keeps the no-dependency hand-rolled dispatch; the registry gives
  Cobra-like help without the framework.

  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--format json|ndjson|text|agent] [--top-k 10] [--deep] [--max-context-bytes 24576] [--head] [--profile syntax-only|fast|full] [--max-indexed-files n|--index-all-files] [--cache-dir path|--no-cache] [--reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card]

  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--file path] [--line n] [--kind kind] [--relation CALLS] [--direction both|in|out] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 20] [--format json|text|agent] [--max-context-bytes 16384] [--head] [--cache-dir path|--no-cache] [--internal-only] [--exclude-tests]

  entire graph stats [--repo .] [--since 30d|7d|all] [--format text|json] [--sessions-dir path|--transcript path]

Notes:

  RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus the other tests that cover the same code (ALSO COVERING —
  they all have to keep passing), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the queried concept is
  named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC — the sweep, so you need no grep), VERIFY (the narrowest test
  command for the file, derived from the repo's own build files) and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a
  switch over an enum/sealed set would throw at runtime rather than fail to compile. The three
  reference blocks — container map, signature types, declaration card — are OFF by default because
  they measurably cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all (or the individual flags,
  or ENTIRE_GRAPH_REFERENCE_BLOCKS) turns them back on for interactive reading.
  search --top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the
  exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every
  eligible file). neighbors/impact take --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME with

Done. Here's what I did.

## Summary

The `entire graph` CLI is a hand-rolled dispatcher with no help framework. Its help was **one dense blob** (a flat `Usage:` list with every flag inlined, plus a wall of `Notes:` prose), and **no subcommand had `--help`** — `search --help`, `neighbors --help`, etc. all errored with "unexpected argument".

I reworked it to match the style of `gh`, the `entire` CLI (Cobra), and `mise`:

**New `internal/cli/help.go`** — a small `commandDoc` registry that is the single source of truth, driving two renderers:
- `renderRootHelp` — a scannable, two-column listing grouped by user intent (exactly the three groups you asked for):
  - **Set up your agent** — `init-agents`, `agent-guide`, `index`, `doctor`, `capabilities`
  - **Inspect the graph** — `search`, `neighbors`, `impact`, `def`, `symbols`, `edges`, `snapshot`
  - **Analyze changes & more** — `commit`, `diff`, `checkpoint`, `stats`, `version`
- `renderCommandHelp` — per-command detail: summary, `Usage:`, a description (the old `Notes:` prose moved to where it belongs), `Arguments:`, aligned `Flags:` (with defaults like `(default: 16384)`), and `Examples:`. Over-long flag placeholders wrap so the description column stays aligned; `analyze` resolves to `diff` as a hidden alias.

**`internal/cli/root.go`** — `printHelp` now delegates to `renderRootHelp`; `Run` intercepts `--help`/`-h` centrally (no per-command changes); the unknown-command error now hints `run "entire graph help"`.

**Tests** — new `help_test.go` enforces registry↔dispatch parity (help can't silently drift from the switch), root grouping/order, and per-command `--help` via `Run`; updated the two existing help-format tests in `root_test.go` and `stats_test.go`.

No command behavior, flag names, defaults, or outputs changed — this is help/UX only. `mise run check` is green.

One thing to flag: `search` has ~15 additional layout-tuning flags (`--context-lines`, `--max-region-lines`, `--body-head-ranks`, etc.) that were never in the old help either. I documented the primary set matching the previous usage line and left the fine-tuning flags out to keep the help scannable — easy to add a "Tuning:" subsection later if you want them surfaced.

Here's the picture, and then two choices I'd like your call on.

**On the JSON:** yes — that final blob is the machine-readable summary, meant for agents/CI/scripts, not really for a human. A script warms the cache and checks e.g. `completeness` to know the graph is trustworthy. For a human it's noise. Both requests done and pushed to **PR #78** (binary is live via the plugin symlink).

## Why "every 1024 files" was wrong

That `1024` was a single hard-coded cadence for emitting progress (each emit runs `runtime.ReadMemStats`, a stop-the-world scan, so it's throttled). The bug: **files and relations differ by ~two orders of magnitude**, but they shared one threshold. Your repo has 374 files, so the parse loop's `(i+1)%1024==0` check *never* fired — you got a single end-of-parse event, hence the 0→374 jump. Relations (33k) crossed 1024 plenty of times, which is why *those* counted up.

Fixed by splitting the cadence:
- **Files** → adaptive `len/100` (floor 1): ~100 updates regardless of repo size, every file on small repos. Verified: your repo now emits **107 incremental parse events** (files climbing 3→372) instead of 1.
- **Relations** → bounded fixed cadence (they stream with no known total, so you can't target a fixed count).

I also made the bar **phase-aware**: it was showing a *full* file bar during the entire relations phase (files pinned at 100%), which looked done while it kept working. Now it's a filled bar + ratio while parsing, then a spinner + climbing relation count while linking.

## `--force`

`entire graph index --force` rebuilds the committed-tree snapshot from scratch and overwrites the cache even when the tree is unchanged. Verified end-to-end: warm→miss, plain rerun→hit, `--force`→rebuild (`built in 32s`, not a hit), and the entry stays refreshed so the next ordinary run hits again. It's threaded via `ProviderSnapshotOptions.ForceRebuild`, which is deliberately **not** part of the cache key — so force refreshes the *same* entry every reader serves (rather than writing a divergent one).

One caveat on verification: I couldn't show the animated bar live because this sandbox's stdin is a socket, so `script` can't allocate a PTY. I proved the mechanics instead — the 107-event cadence above, plus unit tests for the parse bar, relations spinner, and TTY gating. You'll see the smooth animation when you run `entire graph index --repo . --head --force` in your terminal.
